chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Washa, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When a boy reaches his maturity at thirteen years, and enters the fourteenth, it becomes obligatory upon him what is obligatory upon those who have reached puberty, whether he has experienced wet dreams or not. Evil deeds are recorded against him, and good deeds are recorded for him, and everything is permissible for him unless he is weak-minded or foolish.

key_terms.الْمُحْتَلِمِينَ: those who have reached puberty (specifically via wet dreams)

ai.seo_question: What is the age of legal maturity for boys in Shia fiqh according to al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the completion of thirteen lunar years as the threshold for legal maturity (bulugh), marking the onset of religious accountability (taklif) regardless of physical signs like seminal emission. It highlights the Shia juristic principle that while obligations become binding, the individual remains exempt if they lack sufficient cognitive capacity, distinguishing between chronological age and mental maturity.
